pass_meta.suite: Inline Add and Edit Parts on Work Order Lines (6597)

C44993.observed: What was checked: that the Add Part button is taken away once a job is at a stage where it should no longer be changed. What happened: it is taken away on two of those stages and left in place on the third. On a Paid job there is no Add Part button anywhere on the page. On a Complete job there is none either. On a DECLINED job all four Add Part buttons are still on the page and still clickable, exactly as they are on an ordinary open job - and a part added there does save. For comparison, on the same job while it was open and editable the same four buttons were found, so the check does see them when they are there.
C44993.not_observed: Invoiced. A job's stage cannot be moved to Invoiced by hand on this system - the system answers that Invoiced is not a stage you can set, it is reached by raising an invoice - and no invoiced job was available to look at. Imported is not a stage this product has at all.
C44993.todo: What needs to be done: on a Declined job, hide the Add Part button on every job line, the same way it is already hidden on a Paid job and on a Complete job. This is the same underlying problem as the other Declined findings in this suite - a Declined job is still fully editable - so one fix should settle them together.

C44994.observed: What was checked: that the pencil for changing a part already on a job line is taken away once a job is at a stage where it should no longer be changed. What happened: it is taken away on two of those stages and left in place on the third. On a Paid job there are no part-edit controls on the page at all. On a Complete job there are none either. On a DECLINED job all eight are still there, one for each part on the job, and opening one and saving a change goes through. For comparison, on the same job while it was open and editable the same eight were found, so the check does see them when they are there.
C44994.not_observed: Invoiced. A job's stage cannot be moved to Invoiced by hand on this system, and no invoiced job was available to look at. Imported is not a stage this product has at all.
C44994.todo: What needs to be done: on a Declined job, hide the part-edit control on every part row, the same way it is already hidden on a Paid job and on a Complete job. This is the same underlying problem as the other Declined findings in this suite, so one fix should settle them together.

C45022.observed: What was checked: that when saving a new part fails for some reason other than the job being closed to changes - the connection dropping, say - the user is told plainly and does not lose what they typed. What happened: both. Working as a technician, a new part row was opened on a job line and filled in with a description and a quantity, and the save was then made to fail the way a dropped connection makes it fail. A message appeared reading 'Couldn't add the part. Please try again.' The row stayed open with everything still in it - the description and the quantity were both exactly as typed. Nothing had to be re-entered.

C45035.observed: What was checked: that if a job is closed to changes while somebody has a part open for editing, pressing Save is refused and they are told to refresh. What happened: it is not refused. Working as a technician, an existing part on a job line was opened for editing and its quantity changed from 1 to 9. The job was then moved to Declined, which should close it to changes. Save was pressed. No warning appeared - there was no 'This work order can no longer be edited' message and nothing telling the user to refresh - and the row simply closed as though the change had been accepted.
C45035.todo: What needs to be done: when the job is no longer open to changes, refuse the save and show the message 'This work order can no longer be edited. Refresh to see the latest.', leaving what the user typed on screen. This is part of the same Declined problem as the other findings in this suite - a Declined job is still treated as editable everywhere - so one fix should settle them together.

C45058.observed: What was checked: that typing letters, or a negative number, into the cost or the sell price is refused with a message that names the field and says what is wrong. What happened: half of it works. Typing a negative number gives exactly the right message, 'Cost cannot be negative.' Typing letters does not: instead of 'Cost must be a number.' the user is told 'Enter a cost and sell price to save this part.' - which reads as though the boxes were left empty, when in fact they were filled in with something that is not a number. The user is not told what is actually wrong with what they typed. The part is correctly not saved either way.
C45058.todo: What needs to be done: when the cost or the sell price contains something that is not a number, say so in those words - 'Cost must be a number.' and 'Sell price must be a number.' - instead of the message about leaving them empty. The negative-number messages are already right and should not be touched.

C45061.observed: What was checked: that if a job is closed to changes while somebody is part-way through adding a part, pressing Save is refused and they are told to refresh. What happened: it is not refused - the part is added. A new part row was opened on an open job and filled in with a description, a quantity, a cost and a sell price. The job was then moved to Declined, which should close it to changes, and this was read back from the system to be sure it had actually moved. Save was pressed. No warning appeared - there was no 'This work order can no longer be edited' message - and instead the page showed 'Part added'. The part went onto a job that should have been closed to changes.
C45061.todo: What needs to be done: when the job is no longer open to changes, refuse the save and show the message 'This work order can no longer be edited. Refresh to see the latest.', leaving what the user typed on screen. This is the clearest example of the Declined problem running through this suite - a Declined job is still fully editable - so one fix should settle it and the related findings together.

C45062.observed: What was checked: that when saving a new part from the full part row fails for some reason other than the job being closed to changes, the user is told plainly and does not lose what they typed. What happened: both. A new part row was opened on a job line and filled in with a description, a quantity of 3, a cost of 11.50 and a sell price of 22.75, and the save was then made to fail the way a dropped connection makes it fail. A message appeared reading 'Couldn't add the part. Please try again.' The row stayed open with all four values exactly as typed - nothing had to be re-entered.
